svg.text: Module C v2 — Bonus Attachments with Continuous Traverse-Rate Control
Companion sheet to the core blueprint. All dimensions in millimetres. 1 drawing unit = 1 mm.
2 pen holes, r=50 & r=30, rim groove
free axle hole at outer end
seats in rim groove for grip
Scotch-yoke, reused from Module C sine idea
Shared sub-assembly — the Traverse-Rate Unit (used, unmodified, in Modules C2, C3 and C4)
This is the one new part. It replaces every fixed post / fixed leadscrew with a continuously slid-and-clamped
control, the same way the trammel's beam works — read the slot position, that IS the traverse rate.
drive disc Ø100 (ghost — fixed to, and rotates
with, the arm/shaft above this unit)
drive disc underside (rotates; presses lightly on the wheel's tyre)
wingnut — clamps the bracket's slot position only
take-up spool, Ø10, glued to the wheel
idler wheel, Ø16 tyre, free-spins on the sleeve
sleeve — spins freely on the fixed bolt
wide washer (> slot width) stops pull-through
GOVERNING RULE: traverse rate = k·s, where k = R(spool)/R(wheel) = 5/8 = 0.625 (fixed by the parts above).
Spiral growth rate ρ (mm/rad) = k·s. Helix/spiralling-helix pitch (mm/turn) = k·s·2π.
Slot range s=8–45mm gives ρ≈5–28 mm/rad, or pitch≈31–177 mm/turn — read s directly off the scale, no calculation needed.
Build tip: press-fit or epoxy the rubber grommet to a short brass tube for the sleeve; wax the bolt shank so the sleeve spins freely.
Module C2 v2 — Spiral Arm (r = ρ·θ, ρ now set by ONE traverse-rate unit, stepless)
Ø8 pencil hole; eyelet for cord tie
exactly as detailed above — mount its slotted
bracket to the base, centred on the arm's pivot.
Cord runs from the spool straight to the pencil
block's eyelet, along the underside of the arm.
SET-UP: slide the idler wheel to the slot position s that gives your target ρ (read off the scale) and clamp the wingnut.
Tie the cord to the spool, wind 2–3 turns, run it to the pencil block's eyelet and tie off — the taut cord does the rest.
Re-reading ρ later: it's just k×s — no need to unwind anything, the scale is calibrated once and stays valid.
Module C3 — Helix Rig (side view: x=k·θ axial feed + y=r·sinθ crank, both continuously adjustable)
New module — helix never had a physical design before. Main shaft is horizontal; a crank (radius r) drives a Scotch-yoke
(reusing the sine module's own idea) whose carriage is pulled along by a second traverse-rate unit, set for pitch instead of ρ.
Part A — Base rail + pillow blocks
760 rail (adjust to taste — sets max travel)
main shaft: 6mm steel rod, 480–700 long, through both pillow-block holes
Part B — Crank arm (sets coil radius r)
fixed to the main shaft; crank-pin (in the slot)
engages the yoke block's vertical slot below.
identical part to the shared detail above, this
time base-mounted beside the drive disc that's
fixed to the main shaft (not a separate arm).
Cord runs to the axial carriage, Part E below.
gives y = r·sinθ. Pencil mounts on
rides the rail's top edge; yoke's vertical
guide is fixed on top. Cord eyelet (dot)
ties to the traverse-rate unit's spool.
SET-UP: set r on the crank slot (Part B) and pitch on the traverse-rate unit (Part C) independently — they don't interact.
Turn the shaft by hand. The carriage advances by k·s per turn (pitch) while the yoke rocks the pencil through ±r.
Keep the rail and carriage well waxed — this module has the most moving parts in the whole set; friction here shows up as a wobble.
Module C4 — Spiralling Helix Rig (Module C3, with the crank swapped for a second traverse-rate unit)
Build Module C3 in full, then make this one change: replace Part B (the fixed-radius crank) with a second
traverse-rate unit driving a RADIAL slider instead of the crank-pin — now the ‘crank radius’ grows with every turn.
The one changed part — radial traverse-rate unit
same slotted idler bracket as before, but its
spool cord now pulls a RADIAL slider (like the
spiral arm's pencil block) instead of an axial one.
Radial slider rides on a short slotted arm (fixed to the
main shaft, same as Part B was) — but now the cord
continuously pushes it outward as the shaft turns,
instead of it sitting at one fixed radius.
The pin on this slider is what engages the yoke block's
vertical slot (Part D from C3, unchanged).
Two traverse-rate units, two independent slot positions: s(axial) sets pitch, s(radial) sets flare rate — read both off their scales.
Everything else — rail, pillow blocks, main shaft, yoke block, axial carriage — is identical to Module C3. Build C3 first, then adapt it.
